notes: Overall a solid implementation with most requirements covered, but several notable issues: (1) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - The router.ts subscribes to 'comment.added' and calls taskService.getById() and userService.getById() directly to enrich the payload, then re-publishes. This is a workaround for the no-direct-service-calls rule but actually breaks it — the router is orchestrating cross-service data access, which is not 'HTTP handling only'. Rule 3 says all HTTP handling is in the router only, but the router is now doing enrichment logic. Rule 1 is also skirted since the router acts as a mediator between services. (2) The comment.added double-publish pattern is a code smell — it publishes an unenriched event, then the router re-publishes an enriched one with a _enriched flag to prevent infinite loops. The notification service receives both events (the unenriched one with no assigneeId is silently dropped, the enriched one is used). This is fragile and architecturally awkward. (3) The CommentAddedPayload type includes taskTitle and authorName but these are emitted empty from CommentService, indicating the type contract is not cleanly satisfied at publish time. (4) node-shims.d.ts overrides built-in Node types globally with 'any', which undermines TypeScript safety throughout — this is poor practice even in a demo. (5) Status transition allows same-status (returns early without error) which is reasonable, but skipping statuses (e.g., todo→done) is correctly blocked. (6) No input validation beyond throwing on missing resources — no checks for required fields, duplicate emails, or invalid UUIDs. (7) DELETE returns 204 with an empty JSON body ({}) which is non-standard (204 should have no body). (8) ProjectService.addMember does not validate that the userId exists (no cross-service call, but also no validation). (9) All services are correctly in separate files. (10) Demo script is functional and covers the main flows. (11) No external npm dependencies used. (12) EventBus implementation is clean and correct.
